chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) bequeathed to al-Ḥasan, and he made al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), Muḥammad, all of his children, the chiefs of his Shiʿah, and the people of his household witnesses to his bequest. Then he handed over to him the Book and the weapon.

Then he said to his son al-Ḥasan: “O my son, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded me to bequeath to you, and to hand over to you my books and my weapon, just as the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم bequeathed to me and handed over to me his books and his weapon. And he commanded me to command you that, when death comes to you, you should hand it over to your brother al-Ḥusayn.”

Then he turned to his son al-Ḥusayn and said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded you to hand it over to this son of yours,” then he took the hand of his grandson ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn.

Then he said to ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn: “O my son, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم commanded you to hand it over to your son Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, and convey to him greetings from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and from me.”

Then he turned to his son al-Ḥasan and said: “O my son, you are the holder of the authority and the guardian of the blood. So if you pardon, that is for you; and if you kill, then one strike in place of one strike, and you do not sin.”

key_terms.السِّلَاحَ: the weapon, entrusted as part of the legacy of authority
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the Book, meaning the transmitted scripture or written corpus entrusted as a sign of authority
key_terms.ضَرْبَةٌ مَكَانَ ضَرْبَةٍ: one strike in place of one strike, indicating equal retaliation
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الدَّمِ: the one entitled to decide regarding retaliation for blood
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْأَمْرِ: the one vested with authority over the affair

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the transfer of authority and trust from Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) to the later Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the bequest of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) to al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام), including the transfer of the books and weapon as signs of divinely designated authority. It also describes the succession through al-Ḥusayn (عليه السلام), ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, while concluding with guidance regarding authority over retaliation and pardon.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> bequeathed to Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and there bore witness upon his<sup>asws</sup> bequest, Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and Muhammad, and the entirety of his<sup>asws</sup> children, and the chiefs of his<sup>asws</sup> Shias, and his<sup>asws</sup> family members.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> handed over to him<sup>asws</sup> the Book and the weapons, then said to his<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup> Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son<sup>asws</sup>! Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> instructed me<sup>asws</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should instruct you<sup>asws</sup> when the death presents itself, that you<sup>asws</sup> should hand it over to your<sup>asws</sup> brother<sup>asws</sup> Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> turned towards his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> son<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> and said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> instructed you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> that you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> should hand it over to this son<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> of yours<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>: ‘O my<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> son<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! And Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> instructed you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> that you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> should hand it over to your<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> son<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Muhammad<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, and convey from Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> and from me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, the greetings’.

Then heasws turned towards hisasws son Al-Hassanasws, so heasws said: ‘O myasws sonasws! Youasws are the Master of the Command (Wali Al-Amr) and Guardian of the blood (avenging measws). So if youasws were to forgive, so it is for youasws, and if youasws were to kill (Ibn Al-Muljim), so a strike in place of a strike, and youasws would not be overdoing’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabur from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) made his directive will to al-Hassan (a.s.) and asked al-Husayn (a.s.), Muhammad, all his sons, the leaders among his followers and the whole of his family to bear testimony. He then delivered to him the Book and the Armament.

He then said to his son, al-Hassan (a.s.), “My son, the Messenger of Allah commanded me to entrust you with my directive will. (He commanded me) to deliver to you my books, and my armament just as the Messenger of Allah entrusted me with his directive will and delivered his books and armament to me. He commanded me to command you to deliver them all to your brother, al-Husayn (a.s.) when time for you to leave this world will come.
Then he turned to his son, al-Husayn (a.s.) and said, “the Messenger of Allah has commanded you to deliver it all to your son, this one. He then held with his hand Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.)

and said to him, “My son, the Messenger of Allah has commanded you to deliver it all to your son, Muhammad ibn Ali (a.s.) and convey to him the Islamic greeting of the Messenger of Allah and my Islamic greeting.”

He then turned to his son, al-Hassan (a.s.) and said, “My son, you are the Leader with Divine Authority and the authority in the matter of the spilled blood. Were you to forgive it would be for you. Were you to retaliate then one strike for an strike you would not be in sin.”
